end.summary:
Practised finding tens-number partners that make 100, including 30 + 70 and 60 + 40.
Vihaan used tens language: 6 tens and 4 tens make 10 tens, or 100.
Practised number-line jumps and pairs such as 65 + 35 and 48 + 52.
Some partner answers were right, but the method was not steady yet; check more number-line jumps next time.
end.parentNote: Asha practised making 100 with tens numbers and using jumps on the number line. Vihaan used place-value language for 60 and 40, and later corrected the 48 + 52 explanation by matching 4 + 6 and 8 + 2 to make tens. Some number-line items were still uncertain, so at home, ask them to draw a 0–100 line and show the jumps from 48 to 52 and from 60 to 40.
